summary.en: Liouville's theorem says that as a cloud of representative points in phase space (each one a whole system's position and momentum coordinates) evolves under Hamilton's equations, the density of points around any given one stays constant — the cloud's shape can stretch and fold arbitrarily, but its phase-space volume never compresses or expands, exactly the property that lets statistical mechanics treat probability as conserved along a trajectory rather than something that has to be tracked separately.
summary.et: Liouville'i teoreem ütleb, et kui esinduspunktide pilv faasiruumis (igaüks neist on terve süsteemi asend- ja impulsskoordinaadid) areneb Hamiltoni võrrandite järgi, jääb punktide tihedus mistahes punkti ümbruses konstantseks — pilve kuju võib suvaliselt sirutuda ja voltuda, kuid selle faasiruumi ruumala ei kahane ega paisu kunagi; just see omadus lubab statistilisel mehaanikal käsitleda tõenäosust trajektoori pikuti säilivana, mitte eraldi jälgitava suurusena.
